title: Longest Mirror From Two-Letter Tiles
statement:
You have a bag of tiles. Each tile in words holds exactly two lowercase letters. Pick some tiles, each at most once, and lay them in a row in any order to form one string.

Return the length of the longest string you can build that reads the same forwards and backwards. If none can be built, return 0.

examples.why: "ab" + "cc" + "cc" + "cc" + "ba". The pair ab/ba wraps the outside, two "cc" tiles mirror each other, and the third "cc" sits alone in the middle.
Each double tile is a palindrome by itself, but only one tile can be the unmatched center.
"mn" + "nm". The second "mn" has no partner left, and "mn" is not a palindrome alone.

constraints: words[i] has only lowercase English letters
hints: A tile like "ab" can only appear in the answer if a "ba" sits in the mirrored position. What about a tile like "cc"?
Count tiles. Each ab/ba pair adds 4 letters. Each pair of identical double tiles (cc, cc) also adds 4.
After pairing, at most one leftover double tile can go in the exact middle for 2 more letters.

explain.intuition:
In a palindrome built from two-letter tiles, tile number i from the left must be the reverse of tile number i from the right. So tiles come in mirrored pairs: "ab" needs a "ba", and a double like "cc" needs another "cc".

The only exception is the middle tile when the count is odd. It must be its own reverse, so it has to be a double tile. That means: pair up everything you can (4 letters per pair), then if any double tile is still unpaired, add 2 for the center. Only one center is allowed, no matter how many leftovers there are.
steps: Keep a count of unmatched tiles.
For each tile, look up its reverse among the unmatched tiles. If there is one, use it: add 4 and decrease that count.
Otherwise add the tile to the unmatched counts.
At the end, if any unmatched tile is a double (both letters equal), add 2.
pitfalls: Adding 2 for every unpaired double tile. Only one can sit in the middle.
Counting a single "ab" as usable. It is not a palindrome alone.
Pairing a double tile with itself when it appears once, by checking count[reverse] > 0 after adding the tile instead of before.

solutions.title: Match as you go
solutions.idea: Scan tiles once. A tile whose reverse is waiting forms a pair; otherwise it waits. Any waiting double tile can be the center.

solutions.title: Count first, then pair
solutions.idea: Count every tile in a 26×26 table. Mixed tiles pair with their reverse; doubles pair with themselves, and one odd double can be the center.

followups: Return one longest palindrome string, not just its length.
Tiles can now have any length. Why does the simple pairing argument stop working?
lcTitle: Longest Palindrome by Concatenating Two Letter Words
